text:
Sam: Heads-up — I sketched an "acceptance SLA" proposal for model onboarding. Goal: make quick pass/fail checks *fast* and keep longer benches asynchronous. Wanted to get thoughts.

Tanya: thanks — high level sounds good. can you paste the thresholds you had in mind? :eyes:

Sam: sure. initial thought:
- smoke (30s): sanity, load, basic tokenization, kv-cache warmup
- perf-smoke (2-5m): p50/p95 latency on representative prompts (batch=1, seqlen=128)
- quality-smoke (2-5m): small golden set, pass if embedding cosine >= 0.92 or generation BLEU/ROUGE within delta
- fullbench (hours): stratified bench for throughput, mem, tail-latency, regression tests

Leo: +1 on splitting fast vs full. question: where do quantized variants land? they sometimes fail smoke due to numeric drift.

Sam: good point. proposal: allow a "tolerated-drift" path for quantized builds — they get a graded signal (WARN) instead of hard FAIL on first smoke, and get scheduled for fullbench asap. also require a golden-corpus similarity metric to ensure semantics preserved.

Maya: how do we encode results for downstream routing? we need a consistent handshake for the runtime to decide fallbacks.

Sam: interface suggestion: onboarding API returns a JSON-like blob (structured string in registry) with keys: pass/fail, signal-tags (latency_ok, embedding_ok, drift_warn), artifact links (bench logs, golden diffs), numeric metrics. runtime policy can then map tags -> routes. example: `signal-tags: ["latency_ok","drift_warn"]` -> prefer full-precision fallback at high-sla customers.

Tanya: love the signal-tags idea. tiny nit: keep the smoke thresholds configurable per model-class. e.g., small LLM vs embedder vs reranker.

Leo: agree. also we should capture seqlen distribution and typical request batch sizes as part of metadata. that's often why p95 balloons.

Sam: noted. metadata bundle: model_class, quantization, seqlen_percentiles, typical_batch, hw-profile, container-image, registry-link.

Maya: ops concern: fullbench is expensive. who pays? propose we run fullbench on dedicated commit nodes and charge teams the GPU-hours if they request fast turnaround. otherwise queued into weekly batch.

Tanya: fair. also suggest a "canary window" after onboarding where we route small fraction of real traffic and collect production metrics for 24-72h before marking GA.

Sam: yep — canary + automatic rollback on key metric regression.

ingest-bot: automated note: added /onboard/acceptance-sla draft to docs (link: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/sla-draft).

Leo: next concrete step? I can author an RFC that: defines smoke vs fullbench matrix, signal-tags taxonomy, onboarding API contract, and cost model.

Tanya: assign to Leo, cc Sam and Maya. include examples for embed vs autoreg gen.

Sam: sounds good. target: RFC ready in 1 week. owners: Leo (RFC), Maya (ops cost model), Tanya (quality thresholds). I'll spin up the golden-corpus starter set. :thumbsup:

Maya: i'll sketch the canary gating playbook.

Leo: will do. thanks all.
